# MiniMax's Latest Text Model M3.1-Flash-Preview Officially Launched Official Synchronization of Quota Reset Cards and Double Points Rewards
#### AIbase基地
Efficiency competition in the field of large AI models is intensifying again. MiniMax officially announced on September 27 that its latest text model, M3.1-Flash-Preview, is now fully available on the MiniMax Code platform.

To thank developers for their support, the official released a major benefit on the launch day - the quota reset card, which resets all users' Token Plan quotas, and also launched multiple benefits such as free token collection.

Regarding core capabilities, M3.1-Flash-Preview is positioned as a stable productivity tool for daily development work. Whether it's regular bug fixes or complete feature development from scratch, the model can deliver reliably. It not only has the ability to deeply understand complex requirements, but also carefully handles various edge cases (boundary conditions), automatically completes regression testing, and strictly verifies the potential impact of code changes on existing functions.

By organically connecting all aspects, including problem identification, code implementation, testing verification, and result delivery, the model builds an efficient and reliable development loop for developers.

In addition to the iterative upgrades of the core model features, MiniMax also announced that the limited-time "Double Points for Check-in" activity will officially start on September 28 and end on October 7. During this period, all new and existing users who log in to the MiniMax Code platform and complete daily check-ins can easily claim double free points, further reducing the cost of using the platform for developers.

snippets:
# M3.1 has strong potential to be the most cost-efficient large model ahead
I’ve gone through the technical specs of Minimax M3, and I want to share my analysis here.

• Its total parameters are twice the size of last year’s M2.x lineup, which gives it a strong base for complex logical reasoning.

• Compared with other mainstream commercial LLMs, M3 uses a smaller overall parameter size, meaning cheaper costs for inference and deployment.

• The biggest structural change is sparse attention, a design that fits perfectly with the agent tools developers are building nowadays.

• Where it struggles right now is real-world usage, especially coding. The model performs far worse than its hardware/parameter specs promise. The dev team still has lots of tuning work left, so future updates should bring clear performance upgrades.

Even with all these technical strengths, Minimax is in a tough spot right now.
Users’ opinions of M3 have gotten much worse lately. The time Minimax has to patch M3’s issues and win back user trust is running out quickly
